title: The horns that scattered Judah will be cast down (Zech 1:18–21)
speaker: The angel who talked with Zechariah
description: The powers that scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem will be terrified and cast down by four craftsmen.
in_text_interpretation: The horns are "the horns of the nations" that scattered Judah; neither horns nor craftsmen are named.

interpretations.label: The four empires of Daniel: Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece, Rome
proponents: C. F. Keil (1868), with Jerome, Abarbanel and Hengstenberg
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: horns for kingdoms recall Dan 7:7–8 and 8:3–9; four horns seen together can stand for empires that followed one another (as the four beasts of Dan 7). Objection: Mitchell argues that no four specific powers can be identified for the dispersion Zechariah had in view, and Greece and Rome had not yet acted.

interpretations.label: All the hostile powers that brought about the Judean dispersion; "four" for completeness
proponents: Rashi ("the Babylonians at the four winds of heaven"), as reported by Mitchell
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: the context (1:12) concerns the dispersion of Judah after Nebuchadnezzar; since the Jews had more than four adversaries but none of the Babylonians' class, four specific powers cannot be identified, and the number expresses totality. "Israel" in 1:19 is doubtful because 1:21 omits it.

referents.referent: The nations hostile to Judah, chiefly Babylon
